claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode locks a stage to one execution at a time.

CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode only protects an execution once it is actually running, so a newer execution can overtake one that is still waiting to enter a locked stage and drop it before it ever starts.

If a CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up` and enough commits land while it is busy, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.
Setting a CodePipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` causes waiting executions to form a queue so each one runs in turn rather than a later commit erasing an earlier one that never got its turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline.
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline, either via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline`/`update-pipeline` commands or as code.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` Pulumi resource exposes `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is documented at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.

Configuring a CodeBuild project or CodePipeline source stage to trigger on git tag events rather than branch pushes makes promotion a single, traceable Git operation, and ensures production never deploys from an untested commit.
If two Pulumi runs reach the same stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to one of two concurrent runs targeting the same stack, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines can prevent concurrent-run stack conflicts at the source with an exclusive lock check on the environment a deployment job targets.
In Azure Pipelines, the exclusive lock check is added from an environment's "Approvals and checks" tab.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior` is a property set on the stage that references the environment's exclusive lock check.
The Azure Pipelines `Pulumi@1` task accepts a `command` input (e.g. `up`), a `stack` input, and an `args` input (e.g. `--yes`).
In Azure Pipelines, the default value of the `lockBehavior` stage property is `runLatest`.
With Azure Pipelines' `runLatest` lock behavior, only the most recently queued run ever acquires the lock, so an older run stuck waiting behind it is passed over rather than eventually applied.
With Azure Pipelines' `sequential` lock behavior, every queued stage runs against the lock in order, one at a time.
Azure Pipelines' `sequential` lock behavior serializes updates the same way Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack.
The Azure DevOps provider's `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource can be used to manage the Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check as code.

If two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once (e.g., a scheduled build overlapping a manual one, or two commits triggering back to back), Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When Pulumi Cloud grants a stack's update lease to only one of two concurrent build runs, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's own default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as it has available.
TeamCity's default concurrency behavior does nothing on its own to stop a race between two builds targeting the same Pulumi stack.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option called 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under that configuration's General Settings.
TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' advanced option defaults to 0, meaning unlimited simultaneous builds.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first build instead.
When TeamCity's build concurrency limit is set to 1, a queued second build runs only once the first build finishes.

Setting TeamCity's concurrent-build limit to 1 produces the same one-at-a-time behavior that Pulumi Cloud's own per-stack lease enforces, but applied earlier so the build never gets far enough to hit the update conflict.
Pulumi offers native version-control integrations for popular Git hosts, independent of TeamCity.
When a Pulumi version-control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud posts infrastructure-change summaries as pull request comments and status checks.
When a Pulumi version-control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud links each stack update back to the commit and pull request that produced it.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment a deployment job targets, with lockBehavior: sequential on the stage, serializes deployments so they do not run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check that can be added to the environment targeted by a deployment job.
Azure Pipelines supports a lockBehavior setting on a stage, which can be set to the value sequential.
AWS CodePipeline has a pipeline execution mode setting that can be set to QUEUED.
Setting AWS CodePipeline's execution mode to QUEUED causes waiting executions to run in turn (serialized) instead of the default behavior.
AWS CodePipeline's default (non-QUEUED) execution mode lets a newer pipeline execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
TeamCity build configurations support a 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' setting that can be set to 1 to prevent concurrent deployment builds.
